newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian marchioness enlists husband in fur campaign.
newsitem.headline: Italian marchioness enlists husband in fur campaign.

text.p: Posters showing a marchioness and her husband naked in bed were plastered across Italian billboards on Friday in a campaign to dissuade women from wearing fur and men from giving fur as presents.
Marina Ripa di Meana and her husband Carlo are seen pitying the fur-wearing community while in a naked embrace under bedsheets.
"Poor little things, they buy furs because they have no one to keep them warm," Marina is pictured saying.
The campaign is being run by the Italian branch of animal activists' group the International Animal Welfare Fund (IFAW).
Last year's poster campaign featured Marina alone, her arms folded beneath her chest and her pubic hair visible over the slogan: "The only fur I'm not ashamed to wear".

Carlo, once a leader of Italy's Greens Party and a former European environment commissioner, said he decided to take part in the campaign to remind Italian men of their responsibility in buying furs for their partners.
"Too often it is the husbands, or the lovers, who give their partner a fur because they are incapable of giving true love, warmth and affection," he said in a statement.
The 53-year-old Marina added that she had worn furs in the past but had given them up when she "found peace and a new kind of relationship" with Carlo.
Marina said last year she was inspired by Lady Godiva, who rode naked through the English city of Coventry in the 11th century to persuade her husband to cut taxes.
